intro: Grybiskes maps one tree: an oak in a state forest inside Dieveniskes Historical Regional Park, at the foot of which Lithuania's largest recorded porcini mushroom was found in 1971. It placed sixth of thirteen in the country's 2023 national Tree of the Year vote, one place behind the famous Stelmuze Oak. Published alone here because the tree is the destination, not because Grybiskes's research is finished.
meta_description: The Grybiskes Oak: sixth in Lithuania's 2023 Tree of the Year vote, and the site of the country's largest recorded porcini mushroom.
question_meta: Grybiskes's only mapped tree is the Grybiskes Oak, sixth-placed in Lithuania's 2023 national Tree of the Year vote.
question_answer: Grybiskes's only mapped tree is the Grybiskes Oak, a pedunculate oak in the Nemkamedis forest of Dieveniskes Historical Regional Park, about 4.98 metres round, which placed sixth of thirteen entries in Lithuania's 2023 national Tree of the Year vote.
question_context: The tree stands in the Nemkamedis forest inside the Dieveniskes Historical Regional Park, about 26 metres tall, with a trunk of 4.98 metres round at chest height according to the park directorate and 4.93 according to the national arboriculture centre. It has been a state natural monument since November 1999. In 2023 Lithuania ran a national Tree of the Year vote and this oak came sixth of thirteen on 412 votes, one place behind the Stelmuze Oak, the most famous tree in the country. The largest porcini mushroom ever recorded in Lithuania was found at its foot in 1971, weighing 3.05 kilograms with a cap 49 centimetres across, and it is registered in the national book of records. Enough people were coming that in 2016 a platform was built around the base to keep boots off the root plate. Nobody has dated the tree: local sources say around a thousand years, which is lore rather than measurement, and a trunk under five metres round is slim for that kind of age. The walk in is about three kilometres of marked forest trail from the village of Poskonys, with no gate and nobody to ask.

trees.story:
The largest porcini ever recorded in Lithuania was found at the foot of this oak. That was 1971, the mushroom weighed 3.05 kilograms with a cap 49 centimetres across, and it went into the national book of records.

The tree it grew under is the reason people walk out here now. It stands in the Nemkamedis forest inside the Dieveniškės Historical Regional Park, about 26 metres tall, with a trunk of 4.98 metres round at chest height according to the park directorate and 4.93 according to the national arboriculture centre, which measured on a different day. It has been a state natural monument since November 1999.

In 2023 Lithuania ran a national Tree of the Year vote and this oak came sixth of thirteen on 412 votes, one place and 93 votes behind the Stelmužė Oak, which is the most famous tree in the country.

Enough people were coming that in 2016 a platform was built around the base to keep boots off the root plate.

Nobody has dated it. Local sources say around a thousand years, which is lore rather than measurement, and a trunk of under five metres is slim for that kind of age. If you know what has actually been measured here, tell us.

The walk in is about three kilometres of marked forest trail from the village of Poškonys, and there is no gate and nobody to ask.
